venues.d: The capital's palace — gold-domed, ceremonial, and now in the surest of hands.

venues.n: The St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort
venues.d: A long, protected beach and butler service — the calm cultural island, done grandly.

venues.n: Four Seasons Hotel Abu Dhabi at Al Maryah Island
venues.d: The surest hands in the city — service you never have to think about.
A sky-bridge suite slung between two towers, with its own beach club below.
A landmark tower address on the Corniche, polished and quietly capable.
A glass tower on the financial island, run with Rosewood's understated grace.
Sleek, low and sustainable, opening straight onto a protected white beach.

venues.n: Park Hyatt Abu Dhabi Hotel and Villas
venues.d: A low-rise beach house with room to breathe — the quiet Saadiyat choice.

venues.n: The Ritz-Carlton Abu Dhabi, Grand Canal
venues.a: Grand Canal / near Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
venues.d: A Venetian-styled canal palace facing the great white mosque.
Ian Schrager cool on the marina — the city's most design-literate address.
Framed views straight across the water to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque.

venues.n: Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri, Abu Dhabi
venues.d: A souk, waterways and abras — a resort village beside the Grand Canal.
A private island of villas, reached only by boat — the quietest luxury near the capital.

venues.n: Al Wathba, a Luxury Collection Desert Resort & Spa
venues.d: A closer, gentler desert escape — dunes and a serious spa within easy reach of the city.
A dependable beach resort on the cultural island, generous with space.
Modern Emirati cooking beside the city's oldest fort — a taste of the real capital.
The Cantonese standard-bearer, holding its star inside the palace.
Precise, classical sushi that has quietly held its star.
Riviera cooking and a room that never goes out of fashion.
A waterfront pizzeria and bakery that became the city's happiest table.
Beachfront Japanese with real polish — and a business lunch worth crossing town for.
A warm, generous kitchen at the water's edge — a Bib for the bill and the cooking both.
Emirati seafood at the working harbour — Michelin's Opening of the Year.
Levantine cooking done with heart, kept honest by the Bib inspectors.
Gulf and Emirati home cooking with a devoted local following.
Beachfront Lebanese — bright, generous and full every night.
Japanese comfort food at the waterfront, credentialed and easy to love.
Armenian-Lebanese cooking with real character — a Bib regular.
The izakaya template that set the tone for the region — still full every night.
Vivid Peruvian cooking and a room built for a good night out.
Refined North Indian dining with a Grand Canal view of the great mosque.
Contemporary Indian by the Corniche, considered and well-kept.
Playful, modern Indian from a well-loved kitchen.
Polished Italian in the Four Seasons — dependable and quietly grand.
A 1920s-Chicago chophouse — serious steak and a serious bar.
Cantonese comfort cooking with genuine soul, on Al Maryah Island.
Seafront Lebanese from the Em Sherif name — generous and glamorous.
The Venetian classic — Bellinis, carpaccio and a room that knows its worth.
Parisian brasserie dining beneath the Louvre's dome.
Classic French cooking by a Burgundy chef, beside the Grand Canal.
Warm Tuscan cooking in a handsome St. Regis room.
Modern Greek by the beach — bright, sunlit and generous.
Levantine cooking with a sea view on the cultural island.
Nikkei cooking — Japanese precision with a Latin pulse — by the beach.
Elevated Lebanese with a Corniche view — glamorous and assured.
A steak-and-view room on the 62nd floor — the city laid out below.
An over-water seafood house that has quietly kept its following for years.
Pick your catch from the ice and have it cooked to order, by the marina.
Refined Chinese cooking in a serene canal-side room.
Vietnamese cooking in a lantern-lit room — gentle and quietly excellent.
Thai cooking with real fragrance and fire — a long-standing local favourite.
Homestyle Emirati cooking from a young local kitchen — warm and honest.
Emirati family recipes served like a home lunch — the real thing.
Singaporean-Malaysian coffee-shop cooking, done with real affection.
Playful pan-Asian plates at the waterfront — easy, modern and fun.
A plant-forward kitchen doing bright, vegetable-led cooking with intent.
The Arab world's first universal museum — Jean Nouvel's floating dome, and its rain of light, are reason enough to come.
The white marble heart of the capital — 82 domes, a courtyard of inlaid flowers, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet within.
The working Presidential Palace, opened to the public — a domed hall of gold and mosaic, and a library of 50,000 titles under it.
A building made only for teamLab — 17,000 square metres of light, water and air that become the artwork. The children will not forget it.

venues.n: The Empty Quarter — Qasr Al Sarab
venues.d: The largest continuous sand desert on earth, met from a fortress of dunes — dawn walks, falconry, and a silence you feel.
Frank Gehry's largest Guggenheim of all — the anchor of the cultural district, arriving on Saadiyat.
Home of the season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix — Formula 1's first day-to-night race, run under the arch of the Yas hotel's shifting light.
The world's first Ferrari-branded park, under its vast red roof — and Formula Rossa, still one of the fastest launch coasters ever built.
A new-generation marine park with no orcas — eight ocean realms and a research centre, built around one of the world's largest aquariums.
The green lung of the coast — a boardwalk and kayak trails threading a protected mangrove forest, with flamingos and herons at the water's edge.
Eight kilometres of manicured waterfront — the capital's promenade, with a Blue Flag beach and the skyline laid out across the Gulf.
A protected white-sand coast where hawksbill turtles still nest — the calm, wild edge of the cultural island.
The oldest stone building in the city — the 1761 watchtower and fort where Abu Dhabi began, now a museum of its own story.
A fully indoor, fully air-conditioned world of Gotham and Cartoon Junction — a summer-proof day for families.
An Emirati-themed water park built around a pearl-diving legend — record-holding rides and gentler pools side by side.
The whole capital from the air — the great mosque, the islands and the mangrove maze in a single sweep.
The capital's highest bar — Level 62, the whole city and Gulf laid out below, cocktails to match the view.

venues.a: The St. Regis Abu Dhabi, Corniche
venues.d: Three open-air terraces on the St. Regis roof — Mediterranean plates, jazz, and an uninterrupted sweep of the Corniche.

venues.a: The St. Regis Abu Dhabi, Corniche
venues.d: A polished seafood room below, a late, lively rooftop above — a favourite last stop of a big night on the Corniche.
The only rooftop over Yas Bay — the Buddha-Bar signature of low light, deep house and Asian-Mediterranean plates.
The izakaya template for the region, and its bar is among the city's finest — a crowd, a resident DJ, and drinks done properly.
A day-to-night poolside lounge on the financial island — sculptural, easy, and quietly Rosewood-run.
A refined lounge and bar high in the Etihad Towers — a considered list and a considered crowd, above the Corniche.
The biggest indoor club in the country — 360-degree projection, a serious sound system, and the graffiti wall out front.
